prompt: Human: Is there a big difference between the temperature at night and during the day at this time of year?
response:
There certainly can be, depending on where you are and what time of day you are referring to.  Try running these queries:

```
SELECT (t1.time + t1.temperature_8am - t2.time) as time_diff,
       (t1.time + t1.temperature_8am - t2.time) as day_diff
FROM table1 t1
JOIN table2 t2
ON t1.id = t2.id AND
      (t1.time - t2.time) < 3600
WHERE t1.time BETWEEN '2015-09-01 02:00:00' and '2015-09-01 03:00:00'
ORDER BY time_diff DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

```
SELECT (t1.time + t1.temperature_8am - t2.time) as time_diff,
       (t1.time + t1.temperature_8am - t2.time) as day_diff
FROM table1 t1
JOIN table2 t2
ON t1.id = t2.id AND
      (t1.time - t2.time) < 3600
WHERE t1.time BETWEEN '2015-09-01 02:00:00' and '2015-09-01 03:00:00'
ORDER BY day_diff DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

If you run both of these queries you get the following results:

[![Table results via SQL Fiddle](https://i.stack.imgur.com/a7bOw.png)](http://sqlfiddle.com/#!6/f4c3f/1)

As you can see, daytime and nighttime are about 10 degrees cooler.  There are a few cases where 10 degrees at night might not be the lowest temperature (like in the morning and afternoon, or in the cold and hot seasons), but for most places in the northern hemisphere the difference is noticeable.
